To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the FDTD method is an effective technique for modeling electromagnetic phenomena in the Earth-ionosphere cavity and for calculating the electrokinetic effect of earthquakes.

1) The electrokinetic current source is an important component of the Loma-Prieta earthquake source model; 2) the entire Earth FDTD technique is an effective tool for calculating the global propagation of electromagnetic waves generated by the electrokinetic current; and 3) the electrokinetic source is a plausible candidate for the generation of electromagnetic signals associated with the Loma Prietas earthquake.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the propagation of electromagnetic waves through the Earth-ionosphere waveguide, with particular attention to the effects of electrical conductivity and anisotropy of the Earth’s crust and upper mantle.

the development of numerical methods for the solution of Maxwell's Equations in complex geometries, and with the application of those numerical methods to the solution of problems in electromagnetics.

the development of numerical techniques to simulate electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation within the Earth-ionosphere cavity for the purpose of detecting and localizing pre-seismic electromagnetic signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FDTD model of this study is a very useful tool for modeling electrokinetic effects of the Loma-Prieta earthquake.
the FDTD results are in excellent agreement with the analytical and measured spectra.
the FDTD results for the Loma Prierta earthquake are qualitatively similar to previous results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new technique for modeling the electromagnetic fields produced by earthquakes and volcanoes.
the electrokinetic currents calculated by our FDTD model agree well with those calculated analytically.
we have developed a computational technique to model the electromagnetic response of the Earth-ionosphere cavity to impulsive current excitation sources within the Earth's crust and mantle.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the entire-Earth FEM solution to the full Maxwell equations can accurately calculate electrokinetic effects associated with the Loma Priertaftershock sequence, and that this method can be applied to any other earthquake or volcanic source.
it is possible to solve Maxwell's equations for the entire Earth, and that it is possible for the electromagnetic field generated by a seismic event to be detected on the Earth's surface.
the electrokinetic effect is a real phenomenon and can be modeled using Maxwell's equations.
